title: ZeroDeck Cross-Cutting System Requirements
scope: Cross-capability system and operational product requirements applying across ZeroDeck web and Android; excludes capability-specific implementation details and technology/architecture selection.

statements.text: The system MUST resolve the same ZeroDeck account principal across supported web and Android sessions when the user signs into the same account.
The system MUST communicate material differences in capability, permission, availability, or data access between web and Android before the user relies on an affected operation.
The system MUST enforce protected account, entitlement, owner-activation, and administrative authorization decisions at a trusted service boundary rather than relying solely on client-supplied state.
The system MUST preserve active Pro entitlement and owner-controlled activation as independent prerequisites for every MVP-03 provider/API call.
The system MUST deny newly evaluated protected operations after the authoritative service has recorded revocation of the relevant access, entitlement, permission, or owner activation.
The system MUST associate each category of personal, file-derived, URL-derived, account, and operational data it processes with a documented product purpose and authorized access boundary.
The system MUST disclose data to an external service only to the extent required for the user-requested operation and permitted by the applicable product contract and user notice.
The system MUST provide a documented lifecycle policy for each category of system-managed user data, including purpose, retention trigger, deletion behaviour, and exceptions.

The system MUST prevent private credentials, signing material, provider secrets, and other server-only secrets from exposure through public client configuration, user-facing responses, or ordinary diagnostics.
The system MUST validate required operational configuration before enabling the affected capability and fail closed when that configuration is missing, malformed, or inconsistent.
The system MUST keep development, test, and production credentials, data, and operational controls distinguishable and prevent non-production values from authorizing production operations.
The system MUST NOT report a dependent operation as successful when a required service or dependency has failed, timed out, or returned unusable data.
The system MUST limit the user-visible impact of a failed optional or independent dependency to capabilities that require that dependency.
The system MUST define which backend-managed records are recoverable from service or storage failure and identify consequences when recovery is not possible.
The system MUST verify integrity and authorization context of restored backend-managed state before using it to authorize protected operations.
The system MUST retain an appropriately access-controlled record of administrative changes affecting account access, entitlement, owner activation, or protected capability availability.
The system MUST exclude raw credentials, secret values, unnecessary file contents, and unredacted sensitive URL components from ordinary application diagnostics.

The system MUST expose sufficient operational health information for an authorized operator to distinguish service unavailability, dependency failure, and capability-specific degradation without exposing user content or secrets.
The system MUST support recording the scope, timeline, affected capabilities, containment action, and resolution status of a material security or availability incident.
The system MUST enforce documented bounds for resource-consuming operations and storage categories before enabling them for general use.
statements.location: ### Requirement ZD-SYS-020 — Bounded shared resource use

statements.text: The system MUST respond to resource exhaustion or overload with an explicit bounded rejection, deferral, or degraded state rather than silently accepting work it cannot safely complete.
The system MUST identify each production-critical external dependency, its purpose, owner, failure impact, and replacement or exit consideration before production reliance.
The system MUST treat data returned by an external dependency as untrusted input and validate it before using it to affect account state, security outcomes, or subsequent operations.
The system MUST define duplicate-request behaviour for each cross-platform state-changing operation so retries do not create unintended duplicate effects.
The system MUST make provenance and intended release identity of production software artifacts verifiable before accepting them as product updates.
The system MUST identify and handle unsupported or incompatible client/service version combinations before executing operations with unsupported semantics or security assumptions.
The system MUST communicate whether a requested capability is available, unavailable, degraded, incomplete, or completed without implying another capability was also performed.
The system MUST identify which system-managed account data can be exported or made available to the account holder and which categories are excluded with a documented reason.
